skill.name: github-workflow-automation
skill.description: Automates GitHub Actions planning with AI swarm commands, workflow templates, CI/CD examples, and repository management guidance.
skill.summary: Guides AI-assisted GitHub Actions workflow generation, optimization, CI/CD automation, and repository coordination.
skill.author: ruvnet

security_audit.summary: Most Markdown backtick detections are formatting false positives, but the skill still presents many executable GitHub CLI, npx, and workflow examples. I confirmed command flows that can run community packages, modify repositories, expose workflow secrets, or deploy automatically. No prompt injection text was found.

remediation.suggestion: Pin exact package and action versions, avoid global alpha installs, and require users to approve package sources before execution.
Make dry-run behavior the default and require manual approvals, branch protections, and environment protections before fixes or deployments run.

remediation.issue: Secrets exposed to broad workflow environments
remediation.suggestion: Pass only required secrets to specific trusted steps, prefer OIDC where possible, and avoid generic API_KEY variables.

remediation.issue: Command-heavy documentation can be executed by agents
remediation.suggestion: Label examples as review-required and add explicit instructions that agents must ask before running gh, npm, npx, or deployment commands.

semantic_findings.title: Unpinned Third-Party Automation Execution
semantic_findings.description: The skill repeatedly instructs users to run community packages with npx and install claude-flow@alpha globally. This creates supply-chain risk because command behavior depends on external package state.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited lines directly invoke npx ruv-swarm and npm install -g claude-flow@alpha, then generate workflow files. The risk is contextual supply-chain execution, not Markdown formatting.

semantic_findings.title: Automated Repository Changes Without Approval Gates
semantic_findings.description: Examples promote self-healing, auto-execution, and auto-optimization commands that can create PRs, deploy, or apply improvements. The guidance does not add human approval or branch protection conditions around these mutations.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited examples directly use auto-fix, auto-execute, and apply-improvements style behavior. These are legitimate automation goals, but approval gates are not shown.

high_findings.title: Unix shell invocation
high_findings.confidence_reasoning: The setup script installs an alpha package globally, invokes gh authentication, creates workflow files, and runs npx generation. Running it directly can mutate the developer environment and repository.

high_findings.title: Generic API/secret keys
high_findings.confidence_reasoning: The workflow example exposes a generic API_KEY secret to the environment of a third-party command context. That can leak credentials if the dependency or workflow step is compromised.

content.user_title: Automate GitHub Workflows with AI Swarms
content.value_statement: GitHub workflows become hard to maintain as repositories grow. This skill provides AI-assisted templates and commands for CI, PR checks, releases, and workflow optimization.
actual_capabilities: Provides GitHub Actions templates for CI, security scanning, deployment, releases, and monorepo builds.
Shows ruv-swarm and claude-flow commands for workflow analysis, PR validation, and repository coordination.
Includes troubleshooting patterns for failed runs, log analysis, performance profiling, and workflow analytics.
Documents best practices for caching, permissions, OIDC authentication, timeouts, and reusable workflows.
Offers setup guidance for GitHub CLI, Node.js, workflow directories, secrets, and runner permissions.
limitations: Requires external tools such as GitHub CLI, Node.js, claude-flow, and ruv-swarm.
Examples can change repository state when copied into real workflows.
Security depends on reviewed workflow permissions, secrets, and package versions.
It is documentation and templates, not a verified executable workflow package.

use_cases.title: Standardize CI Workflows
use_cases.description: Create repeatable CI templates with language detection, test matrices, caching, and performance checks.

use_cases.title: Improve Pull Request Automation
use_cases.description: Coordinate linting, tests, security checks, documentation checks, and PR comments from one workflow plan.

use_cases.title: Plan Safer Release Pipelines
use_cases.description: Draft release, deployment, rollback, and monitoring workflows before adding them to production repositories.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic CI Workflow
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a repository without GitHub Actions.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a GitHub Actions CI plan for this repository. Include build, test, cache, and pull request validation steps.

prompt_templates.title: Optimize an Existing Workflow
prompt_templates.scenario: Improve speed and cost for a current pipeline.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my existing GitHub Actions workflow. Suggest safe caching, parallel jobs, timeout settings, and redundant step removal.

prompt_templates.title: Design PR Validation Automation
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a PR validation workflow with linting, tests, security checks, documentation checks, and a concise PR comment summary.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Multi-Repository Release Automation
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a multi-repository release workflow with version alignment, dependency updates, staged deployment, rollback checks, and approval gates.

output_examples.input: Review my CI workflow for faster pull request validation.
output_examples.output: A prioritized workflow review with slow jobs identified, caching changes suggested, and a safer test matrix plan.

output_examples.input: Create a release automation plan for a Node service.
output_examples.output: A staged release plan covering changelog generation, artifact creation, deployment risk checks, monitoring, and rollback readiness.

output_examples.input: Investigate a failed GitHub Actions run.
output_examples.output: A failure analysis summary with likely causes, impacted jobs, retry guidance, and workflow changes to reduce repeat failures.

best_practices: Review every generated workflow before committing it to a repository.
Pin action versions and package versions before production use.
Use least-privilege permissions and explicit approval gates for deployments.
anti_patterns: Do not run generated setup scripts without reviewing each command.
Do not expose broad secrets to third-party workflow steps.
Do not enable automatic deploy or auto-fix behavior without branch protections.

faq.question: Does this skill create GitHub workflows automatically?
faq.answer: It provides commands and templates that can generate workflows. Users should review all generated files before committing them.

faq.question: Which tools does it rely on?
faq.answer: The examples use GitHub CLI, Node.js, ruv-swarm, claude-flow, and GitHub Actions runners.

faq.question: Can it help with pull request reviews?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes PR validation patterns for tests, linting, security checks, documentation checks, and PR comments.

faq.question: Is it safe to run the setup script directly?
faq.answer: No. Review package sources, permissions, and generated workflow changes before running setup commands.

faq.question: Does it support monorepos?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes monorepo change detection and package build examples for GitHub Actions.

faq.question: Can it manage production deployments?
faq.answer: It can help plan deployment workflows. Production use should include manual approvals, environment protections, and rollback checks.
